title: Backboard Bank Shots
description: Young shooters aim at the top corner of the backboard square from angles near the rim, learning that the board turns many misses into makes.

content.objective: Use the backboard square accurately from the 45-degree angles close to the rim.
content.setup: Two spots on each side of the rim at 45 degrees, about two metres out.
content.organization: Pairs share a basket: one shoots, one rebounds and passes.
instructions: Stand square to the backboard at the right 45-degree spot.
Aim at the top near corner of the square.
Shoot with a soft arc so the ball kisses the board and drops.
Make five, then switch to the left side.
coachingPoints: Look at the top corner, not at the rim.
Soft touch: the board does the work.
Shoot from 45 degrees, not straight on.
commonMistakes: Throwing the ball hard against the board.
Aiming at the middle of the square.
Using the board from straight in front of the rim.
content.safety: Shooters rebound their own ball only when the lane is clear; nobody stands under the rim while others shoot.
variations: Bank shot after a jump stop.
successCriteria: Four of five bank shots made from each side.
Ball hits the board inside the top corner.
content.gameApplication: Bank shots from the angles are the highest-percentage shots for young players around the rim.
